confusions: The skill says a template fits when its title or rules cover the request; CONF-010 template needs table_tags which the workspace lacks, and the skill's recipe requires tags. No guidance on what to do when the required tag is missing and the customer has not yet decided to add it. I chose table-name scopes (PHI-010) instead.

Recipe 'Protect health data' lists templates including CONF-010 and VND-001; the recipe prerequisites assume the customer already has a tag and approved vendors. Unclear whether to skip template rules when prerequisites are missing or write them and let them report.

CONF-012 with a tag that does not exist yet: the skill says never accept a warning that a tag does not exist, but here the tag is the value being required, not referenced. Unclear whether this rule is acceptable before the tag is created. Parse gave no warning.

Severity: `xano policy parse` text output omits the severity line for CONF-012 (medium), while JSON output keeps severity: medium. Looks like a display quirk; I could not tell if medium is a default that is hidden.

The skill says RET-001's audit-call rules need when.tables and when.statement; it does not say whether when.statement accepts only one statement per rule. I wrote one rule per statement (db.add, db.edit, db.patch, db.del) which parses, but that is four rules per policy for one concept.

PHI-020 would find nothing in the current workspace for db.add/db.patch/db.del on these tables; it's coverage for future code. Unclear from the skill whether writing rules that currently match no finding is wanted.

The 'Where values go' section lists debug.log as a log destination, but the LOG-001 template only checks debug.log; the skill says datadog.log needs adding separately. Not relevant here (no datadog.log in workspace) but the template limits text is the only place this is stated.
The HIPAA recipe's access-record rule uses object.statement_required with reaching_table_tags, which needs a tag; no non-tag form is described for access recording.
wished_for: A HIPAA or PHI recipe that works without tags: scope by table names and field names, with a clear statement of which rules need tags and which don't.
A worked example of the object.statement_required when{} selector with one statement, and whether several statements can share one rule.
A check or template for 'every read of sensitive tables is logged' (access logging), since it is a core HIPAA requirement.
Guidance on writing rules whose tag does not exist yet: report until the tag is created, or hold the rule back.
why_confidence: The policies parse and cover the parts that are checkable with the workspace's current names (PHI field marking, login on PHI endpoints, output fields, debug logs, TLS, audit log writes). But HIPAA is mostly about access logging, approved vendors, tags and runtime controls, and none of those are covered. The parse only shows validity, not that the rules match the intended objects. I did not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden in this run), so every expected finding is a prediction.
